instance_description:
Setting: A 2026 consumer-finance workspace for a manufactured-home owner in Enid, Oklahoma, handling ordinary personal money administration outside business or employer accounts.
Scope: Recurring activities include park lot rent, home-loan reminders, utilities, propane, storm-season insurance paperwork, vehicle upkeep, roadside assistance, mail-order returns, appliance warranties, subscriptions, and receipt organization.
Resources: Household records include account and equipment references, standing preferences, service contacts, personal receipts, calendars, and reusable workpads.
Exclusions: No investment trading, tax filing advice, legal strategy, lending applications, employer reimbursement administration, business bookkeeping, or irreversible high-stakes financial commitments.
personal_description:
Identity: Marina Odette Pell is a 46-year-old rural mail carrier who owns a small manufactured home, leases its park lot, drives a personal pickup, and manages her own consumer records.
Responsibilities: She tracks routine home and vehicle expenses, preserves receipts, reviews services, organizes insurance documentation, monitors subscriptions, and follows up on refunds, repairs, and warranty issues.
Authority: Marina can categorize expenses, prepare payment checklists, draft merchant or insurer messages, compare routine vendors, and document consumer follow-ups for her personal household.
Restrictions: She cannot manage postal funds, handle another person’s money, give professional financial advice, bypass account security, trade securities, or authorize actual payments without explicit owner authorization.
